thread:
olivia: Heads-up — canary for dedicated pool serval-prod shows a sudden P95 jump (~220ms -> ~470ms) starting right after the 4821 merge. Holding the rollout. graph: https://redwood-internal/graphs/serval-canary-p95 :warning:

sam: ack. which change in 4821 looks suspicious?

olivia: the merge touched kernel selection weights + introduced a new "prefer_conv_fp32" tie-breaker. it seems scheduler now prefers conv_fp32 for certain batch/sample patterns.

cheng: profiling dump from the canary box (short):
```
2026-01-11T02:13:02Z profile: request_id=req-9a1
seq_len=64, batch=4
kernel_choice: conv_fp32_bias (score=0.912)
alternative: fused_int8_conv (score=0.874)
observed_latency=462ms (baseline expected ~210ms)
kv_cache_hits=72% -> 58% (eviction spike)
```
seems like kernel choice + more frequent KV evictions. :thinking_face:

marco: interesting — I remember conv_fp32 has worse per-token perf on our Ampere tuning. Why would score move that much?

olivia: 4821 changed scoring to add `input_variance_factor` so short bursts with higher variance get higher fp32 score. likely side-effect.

beth: CI-perf flagged something earlier but it was below threshold so merge auto-approved. ci-bot, do you have the failing check?

ci-bot: canary-perf-1 failed on 2026-01-11T01:57: check: p95_latency_increase = +125% vs baseline, regression_size=0.05 (threshold 0.06). Logs: https://ci.redwood/checks/4821-canary-perf

sam: can we bisect down to the subset of commits in 4821? is there a quick repro in staging?

cheng: yes repro on staging with heavy seq variance test — i can run a narrower bisect. will try swapping out the new tie-breaker at runtime and reprof.

oncall-bot: Rolling hold engaged on rollout serval-prod (reason: canary p95 spike). Notifying oncall.

olivia: plan suggestions: 1) revert 4821 immediately (fast, safe) 2) patch scheduler to cap fp32 preference unless sequence length > 256 (targeted) 3) temporary routing fallback to older kernel catalog for dedicated until fix. thoughts?

marco: prefer option 2 + 3 if we can do quick patch — revert impacts other in-flight changes. can we land a hotfix flagging `prefer_conv_fp32=false` via remote flag?

beth: we can flip a remote config on dedicated pools within 5 mins. would mitigate customer impact.

cheng: I'm running the bisect now. if hotflag helps, I'll still open a smaller PR to adjust scoring logic to account for cached-kv ratio.

sam: :thumbsup: flip the remote flag, watch canary for 2 cycles, if green then continue canary with throttled rollout. if still bad, revert.

olivia: flipping flag now: `rdctl config set serval-prod prefer_conv_fp32 false --source emergency`

deploy-bot: rdctl apply succeeded: prefer_conv_fp32=false applied to serval-prod at 2026-01-11T02:22Z

cheng: re-run profile after flag flip — new sample:
```
kernel_choice: fused_int8_conv (score=0.901)
observed_latency=218ms
kv_cache_hits=71%
```
looks back to normal.

olivia: great. leaving hold in place and letting canary run 30m before resuming. filing follow-up: PR to revert scoring change or make it conditional on seq_len histogram + kv_cache_ratio. tagging @eng-runtime and @eng-ml for review.

sam: please add customer impact note for the dedicated SLA run and timeline. we should notify CS for any affected tenants.

beth: adding outage note: "canary detected P95 spike in dedicated pool; mitigated via emergency config flip. rollback PR pending."

olivia: thanks everyone. next steps: cheng to open hotfix PR, beth to notify CS, sam to update rollout plan. leaving thread open for bisect logs. :eyes:
